reply.text:
I can't give you an amount for salt or sodium loading. That falls under supplements, and the right number depends on your body, your sweat rate and your health, so it's one for a doctor or a sports dietitian. Some people have medical reasons to be careful with sodium, which is why I won't throw out a figure.

What I can speak to is the general picture. In heat, the basics matter most: arrive well hydrated, eat normally the days before, and practice your fueling and drinking plan in training so race day holds no surprises. Don't try anything new on race morning. A dietitian can work out a plan from your sweat rate if you want it dialed in.

If you tell me the race date, I can build the training plan around it.
